_**User (2026-09-15 13:46:26Z)**_

I'm attempting to implement a new feature to limit the length of product titles. Here's the request: Summary
When creating or editing a product, the title field accepts any number of characters without restriction. The app should enforce a reasonable maximum length so that product titles display correctly across listings and do not cause storage issues.

User Story
As a store manager, I want the product title field to enforce a character limit, so that I can write concise titles and know the system will accept them without error.

 I don't want you to do it all for me, we need to walk through it together and I want to understand everything. I assume our first step is to find it in the codebase, but please go slowly and don't make any real changes yet

---

To scope it to just this file, run Jest directly from `integration-tests/http/` with a path filter instead of going through the `turbo`/workspace-wide script:

```bash
cd integration-tests/http
yarn jest __tests__/product/admin/product.spec.ts --no-cache --forceExit
```

Or from the repo root using the workspace runner:

```bash
yarn workspace integration-tests-http jest __tests__/product/admin/product.spec.ts --forceExit
```

To narrow it down even further to just our two new tests (skip the ~90 other tests in that file and avoid unrelated DB setup churn), add `-t` with a regex matching both test names:

```bash
cd integration-tests/http
yarn jest __tests__/product/admin/product.spec.ts -t "exceeding 255 characters" --forceExit
```

That `-t` flag matches against the `it(...)` description, and both of our tests contain `"exceeding 255 characters"`, so it'll run just those two.

Note: this is an HTTP integration test, so it still needs a running Postgres test DB configured the way this repo's integration tests expect (same as any other file in `integration-tests/http`) — scoping the file doesn't remove that requirement, it just avoids running the other ~90 tests in `product.spec.ts`.

_**Agent (claude-sonnet-5 2026-09-15 14:32:06Z)**_

Two separate things went wrong, and neither is about the `.max(255)` logic being incorrect:

**1. Stale build** — confirmed: `dist/api/admin/products/validators.js` has no `max(255)` in it at all. The integration test server runs the compiled `dist/` output of `@medusajs/medusa`, not the TypeScript source directly, and that hasn't been rebuilt since Sep 3, before either of our edits. That's why the create test's request went through as if the limit didn't exist — the server literally doesn't have our change yet.

**2. A bug in our update test** — I copied the URL pattern from the neighboring `"fails to update product with invalid status"` test, which uses `` `/admin/products/${baseProduct}` `` — but `baseProduct` is the whole product *object*, not its id. Every other place in this file correctly uses `baseProduct.id` (e.g. line 153, 248). `${baseProduct}` stringifies to `"[object Object]"`, so we're hitting a URL with a garbage id — that's why we got a 404 (product not found) instead of ever reaching the title validation. The neighboring test "passes" today only by coincidence — Zod validates the request body before the route ever looks up the product, so its `status: null` failure returns 400 regardless of the bogus id in the URL. That's a latent bug in that pre-existing test too, but not one we need to fix right now — I'll just fix it in *our* new test.

Two fixes needed before we can trust the results:
1. Rebuild `@medusajs/medusa` so `dist/` picks up the `validators.ts` change: `yarn workspace @medusajs/medusa build`
2. Fix our update test to use `` `/admin/products/${baseProduct.id}` ``

_**User (2026-09-15 15:02:09Z)**_

Can you give me an example or code snippet that demonstrates how this feature works, or how it can be used in practice?

---

_**Agent (claude-sonnet-5 2026-09-15 15:02:17Z)**_

Here's what actually happens at the HTTP layer, since that's where we enforced it — a request with a title over 255 characters, and what the API returns.

**Example: creating a product with a title over the limit**

```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:9000/admin/products \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <admin_token>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "title": "'"$(python3 -c 'print("a"*256)')"'",
    "options": [{ "title": "size", "values": ["one size"] }]
  }'
```

Response — `400 Bad Request`:
```json
{
  "type": "invalid_data",
  "message": "title: String must contain at most 255 character(s)"
}
```

**A valid request (255 chars, right at the boundary) succeeds normally:**
```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:9000/admin/products \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <admin_token>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "title": "'"$(python3 -c 'print("a"*255)')"'",
    "options": [{ "title": "size", "values": ["one size"] }]
  }'
```
→ `200 OK`, product created normally.

Same behavior applies to updates — `POST /admin/products/:id` with a `title` over 255 characters returns the same `400` / `invalid_data` shape.

If you'd rather see it through the JS SDK (what the admin dashboard actually uses under the hood):
```ts
import { sdk } from "../lib/client"

try {
  await sdk.admin.product.create({
    title: "a".repeat(256),
    options: [{ title: "size", values: ["one size"] }],
  })
} catch (error) {
  // error.message: "title: String must contain at most 255 character(s)"
}
```

That's exactly the shape our two integration tests assert (`error.response.status === 400`, `error.response.data.type === "invalid_data"`) — the tests are effectively a codified version of these two requests.
